reason: E1 supports the MLIP+CPA framework for refractory MPEAs but addresses mechanical properties, not electrical conductivity. E2 confirms oxygen contamination near 1 wt.% and its impact on properties, but does not link it to conductivity. E3 shows microstructural inhomogeneity (Ta-rich features) from ab-initio MC, but again without connection to electrical transport. The key premise that including defects improves conductivity predictions over ideal-crystal models is not directly supported by any cited evidence.
premises: MLIPs combined with CPA can predict properties of refractory MPEAs with ab initio accuracy
Oxygen contamination at ~1 wt.% occurs in HfNbTaTiZr and affects its properties
HfNbTaTiZr exhibits microstructural inhomogeneities such as Ta-rich features
Explicit inclusion of defect chemistry and local relaxations improves transport predictions over ideal-crystal models
